statement: The first line holds n and k; the second holds n non-negative integers. Print how many contiguous subarrays have XOR equal to k. The prefix trick carries over because XOR is its own inverse: with pre(i) the XOR of everything up to i, the segment after j ending at i has XOR pre(i) XOR pre(j) - so at each position, add how many earlier prefixes equal pre XOR k. Seed the map with prefix 0 occurring once, exactly as with sums, and the loop is the counting loop verbatim with plus swapped for XOR.

example.why: Four stretches XOR to 6, among them the lone 6 and the full five-element run.

hint: The lookup key is pre XOR k - XOR both sides of the segment identity to see it.
mistake: Looking up pre minus k out of habit; subtraction belongs to sums, the XOR inverse is XOR.
